changes.new_value: The schedule list: Active/Archived tabs, search, row menu

changes.label: Preconditions
changes.old_value:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or any user with "Settings Service" enabled. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on for the shop (it ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance: in the left sidebar under Settings choose "Maintenance" (it sits beneath "Inspection Templates"). Schedules here belong to the location chosen in the header, as canned lines do.
  3. Several schedules exist, at least one active and one archived; some have assets enrolled.
changes.new_value:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or a user with "Settings Service" enabled, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on for the shop (it ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. In the left sidebar under Settings choose "Maintenance" (it sits beneath "Inspection Templates"). Schedules here belong to the location chosen in the header.
  3. Several schedules exist - at least one active with assets enrolled and one archived. Seed them:
  4. Seed a maintenance schedule (standard steps):
  5. ↳ In Settings > Maintenance click New schedule; the "Untitled schedule" editor opens.
  6. ↳ Inline-edit the title to a test name (e.g. "Highway Tractor PM").
  7. ↳ Click Add service, give it a name (e.g. "PM-A") and a calendar interval (e.g. Every 3 months), and save the service.
  8. ↳ Click Save on the schedule.
  9. ↳ To seed an archived schedule, open its row menu and choose Archive.
  10. ↳ Seed a second schedule and enrol an asset on it (asset Maintenance tab -> Enrol) so its Assets count is non-zero.

changes.label: Steps
changes.old_value:
1. Read the list: its tabs and counts, its columns and default sort, and the search above it.
  2. Open the row menu on an active schedule, and on an archived schedule.
  3. Click an archived schedule and try to change something.
  4. Look at how the enrolled-asset count is shown.
changes.new_value:
1. Read the list: its tabs and counts, its columns and default sort, and the search above it.
  2. Open the row menu on an active schedule, then on an archived one.
  3. Click an archived schedule and try to change something.
  4. Read how the enrolled-asset count is shown, and click it.

changes.label: Expected Result
changes.old_value:
Expected results

  • The list has two tabs, Active and Archived, each with a count; columns are Schedule, Services and Assets, each sortable from its header, default Schedule A to Z; a search above the table matches schedule and service names.
  • An active schedule's menu offers Edit, Duplicate and Archive; an archived schedule's offers Restore.
  • Each schedule shows how many assets are enrolled as plain read-only text (like inspection templates), never a badge; the count opens nothing.
  • Clicking an archived schedule opens it read-only all the way down (services, triggers, lines), so a shop can see what it archived before restoring; there is no delete anywhere — a schedule made by mistake is archived, not deleted.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10558 (S1, Create a maintenance schedule); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), Part 1 / S1; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R2: “The schedule list has two tabs, Active and Archived, each with a count. Its columns are Schedule, Services and Assets, and each sorts from its header; the default is Schedule, A to Z. A search above the table matches schedule and service names. An active schedule's menu offers Edit, Duplicate and Archive; an archived schedule's offers Restore”
  • S1-R12: “Each schedule shows how many assets are enrolled on it as plain read-only text, as the inspection templates list does, never as a badge. The count opens nothing”
  • S1-R13: “An archived schedule opens read-only all the way down, its services, triggers and lines, so a shop can find what it archived and see it before restoring it”
  • S1-E1: “A schedule created by mistake is archived, like any other. There is no delete anywhere in the feature and no draft state to abandon”
